findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed learning window is the score-time interval [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing, and the curve support is [0.0, 0.49]; recorded affinities are removed and an equal score prior is used, so no absolute affinity label is observed and last-record credit cannot be read as final affinity benefit.

Continuous contrast features are reported only over the observed support with extrapolation disallowed and observed-node linear fits; the inspected landmark features show multiple sign changes (4 to 10) and strong sign conflicts (1 to 9) with relative node RMSE from about 0.29 to 0.78, so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must stay within the observed nodes.

Whole-window z values for the inspected landmark features are small in magnitude (about -0.58 to 0.64) while first-rate and last-rate z values are large and of opposite sign, indicating that the apparent within-window change is dominated by rate turnover rather than a stable whole-window signed contrast; these are coordinate contrasts, not physical interaction energies.

hypotheses.falsifier: no improvement in whole-window signed contrast fidelity, or new sign conflicts exceeding those already observed, when the time-conditioned rule is compared with the constant rule on the same observed nodes
hypotheses.observable: landmark soft-mass and local second-moment contrast features at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention recipe that follows the validated observed-node contrast changes of landmark soft-mass and local second-moment features, rather than a constant static regional weight, would better track the observed coordinate contrasts within the window [0.0, 0.5].

hypotheses.falsifier: a within-path increment contrast that is stable in sign and magnitude across the window while cohort composition is held fixed
hypotheses.observable: first-rate z, last-rate z and whole-window z of the same landmark features
hypotheses.statement: Because first-rate and last-rate z values have opposite signs while whole-window z is small, the observed change is more consistent with changing cohort composition or turnover than with a stable within-path coordinate drift.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes are supplied, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit and the immediate-selection versus descendant-survival comparison is unavailable.
No covariance, intact-conformation or mode diagnostics were read in this turn, so coherent joint coordinate patterns versus isolated marginal descriptors cannot be compared.
No branch-adjusted, survival, increment, turnover or joint-diagnostic tables were read, so multiplicity-adjusted support, ancestral coverage and survivor bias could not be ranked.
The inspected continuous features are untyped coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world coordinates; they are not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed or evaluated.
